keyVerseText: And the sons of Mishma; Hamuel his son, Zacchur his son, Shimei his son.
rootMeaning: The name חַמּוּאֵל (Chammûwʼêl) derives from the Hebrew words חַמָּה (chammâh), meaning 'heat' or 'sun,' and אֵל (El), meaning 'God.' This composite suggests a literal meaning of 'heat of God' or 'anger of God,' emphasizing a fiery, intense aspect attributed to the divine. The root conveys not just physical heat but also the powerful, consuming presence or judgment of God, adding depth beyond a simple proper name.
usageInScripture: The word חַמּוּאֵל appears only once in Scripture, specifically as a proper name referring to an Israelite man of the tribe of Simeon in 1 Chronicles 4:26. It is consistently translated as 'Hamuel,' indicating its use primarily as a personal name rather than a common noun or thematic term. This singular occurrence highlights its role as a marker of identity within the genealogical record, rather than a broader theological concept.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding חַמּוּאֵל as 'heat of God' or 'anger of God' enriches our appreciation of how names in Scripture often carry theological weight, reflecting attributes of God or His interaction with His people. This name reminds believers that God's presence can be both life-giving and purifying, marked by divine intensity and holiness. For the Christian faith, it points to the reality that God's righteous judgment and passionate love coexist, preparing the way for redemption through Christ. Recognizing the fiery aspect of God in this name encourages reverence and awe toward His sovereign will.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Chronicles 4:26, the name Hamuel appears as part of a genealogical listing: 'And the sons of Mishma; Hamuel his son, Zacchur his son, Shimei his son.' Here, Hamuel identifies a specific individual within the tribe of Simeon, grounding the narrative in historical reality. The meaning 'heat of God' subtly underscores that even ordinary lives within God's people carry the imprint of His power and presence, reminding readers that every generation is encompassed by God's sovereign heat and holiness.
